title: Additive and multiplicative attention
brief: Implement Bahdanau and Luong attention and their backward pass, then hand-build weights that make a decoder copy its source exactly.
hints: additive_attention needs one score per key: stack them as scores[i] = v @ tanh(W1 @ query + W2 @ keys[i]). Vectorise with U = (W1 @ query) + keys @ W2.T, shape (Tx, d), then scores = tanh(U) @ v.
multiplicative_attention with W is scores[i] = query @ W @ keys[i], vectorised as (query @ W) @ keys.T. Without W it needs query.shape == keys.shape[1:] and is just keys @ query.

Backpropagate additive_attention by reversing the vectorised forward: dvalues = outer(weights, dcontext), dweights = values @ dcontext, then the usual softmax-Jacobian trick dscores = weights * (dweights - sum(weights * dweights)).

To emulate a dot product with the additive form, set W1 = W2 = c * I for a small c, and v equal to the query itself. tanh is linear near zero, and the resulting constant offset cancels in the softmax.

For decode_with_attention, position vectors (large multiples of the standard basis) make W1 = W2 = identity and a negative v pick out the matching position: two active entries in tanh(u_i) score lower than one, so the diagonal always wins once the scale is large enough to saturate tanh.
